sections.title: Exhausting Logical Alternatives
sections.content: To demonstrate that an outcome is invariant across two opposite scenarios ('whether A happens or B happens'), Hungarian repeats the conjunction 'akár' before each alternative: 'Akár marad az utas, akár távozik, a pénztár nem zárhat be' (Whether the passenger stays or leaves, the ticket window cannot close).

sections.title: Elliptical 'akár..., akár nem' and 'akárhogy is'
sections.content: When the second alternative is simply the negation of the first, Hungarian uses 'akár..., akár nem' ('Akár tetszik, akár nem' — Whether you like it or not). Furthermore, 'akár-' combines with manner adverbs in fixed analytical idioms: 'akárhogy is nézzük' (however we look at it / either way).

sections.title: Disjunctive Concessive Structures
rows: Whether you have small change or not...
Akár tetszik, akár nem, ez a törvény.
Whether we like it or not, this is the law.
Akárhogy is nézzük, a kérdés jogos.
However we look at it, the question is legitimate.

items.spanish: Akár elfogadjuk az alapfeltevést, akár elvetjük, ugyanoda jutunk.
items.english: Whether we accept the basic premise or reject it, we arrive at the same place.

items.spanish: Akár van vasúti sín az állomáson, akár nincs, a bürokrácia működik.
items.english: Whether there is a railway track at the station or not, bureaucracy functions.

items.spanish: Akárhogy is nézzük, ebből a körből nem lehet kilépni.
items.english: However we look at it, one cannot step out of this circle.

sections.title: B2 Stylistic Notice
sections.content: Unlike English 'whether... or...', Hungarian repeats the exact same word 'akár..., akár...' in both branches (never 'akár... vagy...').
